Diagnose infeasibility in optimization models.
For example, sometimes a constraint cannot be satisfied—such as when total local generation plus imported electricity is still insufficient to meet demand. In those cases, the model simply returns “infeasible,” without immediately revealing which constraint or assumption caused the issue.
column60:
An AI modeling assistant would be genuinely useful if it could understand the structure of optimization models rather than just individual lines of code. For example, being able to trace constraint dependencies, identify potential sources of infeasibility, and suggest systematic debugging strategies would significantly improve modeling efficiency.

It would also be valuable if the assistant could reason about data-model consistency, such as detecting when demand exceeds available generation capacity across regions or time periods before the model is run.

However, it would become unusable if it generated overly confident but incorrect explanations, or suggested fixes without understanding the economic or physical logic behind the model. In large-scale power system models, superficial debugging can easily introduce deeper structural errors.
